name: Sun
headline: diameter
description: The Sun is the star at the centre of our solar system and holds about 99.8% of its mass. NASA puts its diameter at about 1.4 million km (865,000 miles); its volumetric mean radius is 695,700 km, about 109 times Earth's. It is a ball of hot plasma with no solid surface, powered by nuclear fusion in its core.

measures.label: Diameter
measures.note: NASA's rounded figure, also given as 1.4 million km

measures.label: Mean radius
measures.note: Volumetric mean radius; the IAU nominal solar radius is exactly 6.957 x 10^8 m, the same value

facts.text: The Sun's mass is about 332,900 times Earth's, and its volume about 1,304,000 times Earth's.
NASA gives the Sun a radius of about 700,000 km (435,000 miles) and says it would take 1.3 million Earths to fill it.
The Sun accounts for 99.8% of the solar system's mass.
In 2015 the IAU defined the nominal solar radius as exactly 6.957 x 10^8 m, a conversion constant for astronomers rather than a claim about the Sun's true edge.
The Sun's core is about 15 million degrees Celsius (27 million degrees Fahrenheit).

caveats: The Sun has no solid surface; its radius is measured to the visible photosphere.
NASA's diameter is rounded (about 865,000 miles / 1.4 million km); twice the 695,700 km mean radius is the more exact figure.
